A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGDD research work. Their text, equations, nine tables, eight figures and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original experiments on synthetic data, DNA design, MNIST, music infilling and FFHQ super-resolution, together with ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds a DNA-generation comparison with FK-MAX in Table 3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same split Gibbs updates, Hamming-distance regularizer, discrete diffusion prior step, Metropolis-Hastings likelihood sampling and annealing schedule. The score-entropy addition concerns theoretical analysis, without changing the training or sampling procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic grids, HepG2 enhancer design, MNIST reconstruction and conditional generation, monophonic music infilling, and FFHQ super-resolution. The added FK-MAX comparison uses the existing DNA task.

E2.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 3 add FK-MAX, a Feynman-Kac diffusion sampler with a MAX potential, to the DNA comparison. Existing comparator membership in the other experiments, including appendix comparisons, is unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, sample counts, metrics and experimental settings are retained. FK-MAX joins the existing evaluation of 640 DNA sequences without introducing a different evaluation protocol; Appendix C and Table 7 retain the sampler settings.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the same noise-schedule ablation, computing-budget analysis and comparison with sampling without a prior. The sample-diversity examples, MNIST reconstructions and synthetic distribution visualizations are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Uncertainty-reporting practices and seed disclosures are unchanged. The FK-MAX row follows Table 3's existing mean-and-dispersion convention; v3 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds FK-MAX results: median activity 4.90, average activity 4.79 ± 1.02, ATAC accuracy 47.1%, and average log-likelihood -243 ± 9. Existing numerical results and figure content are unchanged, including SGDD's leading activity scores.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 changes the bound from FI_Q(mu||pi) with KL(mu0||pi0) to FI_Qtilde(pi||mu) with KL(pi0||mu0), while retaining the distributions' original roles. Appendix A revises the supporting lemmas and derivations and adds alternative assumption (i') and Lemma 4, bounding a Lagrangian error through score entropy. These substantially revise the guarantee and supporting mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about principled discrete posterior sampling, convergence and superior empirical performance. The headline performance improvements and claimed application scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: The new Appendix A.1 note connects score-quality assumptions to the score-entropy training loss and discusses replacing pointwise error and transition-matrix bounds with an average-loss assumption. Experimental interpretations and the limitations in Appendix E remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C and Tables 6–7 retain the same implementation, hyperparameter and hardware information. V3 prints the full code URL in the abstract, but v2's SGDD hyperlink already points to the same repository; this does not change the reported access information.

R1.justification: The SMC discussion adds works by Chen, Singhal, Skreta and Trippe and removes Cardoso's cited work. Section 3.5 also narrows its criticism from SMC-based methods generally to specific previous methods. The overall positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V3 adds acknowledgments, replaces the preprint footer with NeurIPS 2025 information, expands the displayed code link and makes localized wording and cross-reference edits. The principal section sequence and most explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains the FK-MAX row, and Figure 1 moves from page 3 to page 4. Surrounding text and appendix material reflow, but all eight figures retain their content and the overall table and page design remains similar.

improvement.justification: The added FK-MAX comparison and score-entropy connection provide useful additions. However, the theoretical revision is inconsistent: v3's Theorem 1 reverses the Fisher/KL arguments and changes the generator, while Appendix A.2, Equations (38)–(41), still derives v2's original-direction bound. This unresolved mismatch affects the central convergence guarantee, preventing a reliable net quality judgment despite the limited empirical and positioning improvements.
